question: What are Qnami's main weaknesses? Give short bullet points
answer:
Here are some of Qnami’s main weaknesses, based on available information:

• Niche market focus  
  Qnami’s technology—scanning NV (nitrogen-vacancy) magnetometry—is highly specialized, targeting nanoscale magnetic imaging in fields like materials science, spintronics, and quantum computing. This narrow focus limits its addressable market compared to broader sensing or imaging technologies. ([eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3478991309838724?utm_source=openai))

• High technical complexity and cost  
  The system relies on advanced components—diamond NV centers, lasers, microwave sources, and precision scanning hardware—making it complex and likely expensive to manufacture, maintain, and operate. ([horiba.com](https://www.horiba.com/chn/materials/news/detail/news/6/2021/nv-magnetometry-a-white-paper-by-qnami/?utm_source=openai))

• Limited commercial traction  
  While Qnami has secured Series A funding (~4 million CHF) and expanded into markets like Japan and South Korea, its customer base remains relatively small, with installations primarily in research institutions rather than widespread industrial adoption. ([thequantuminsider.com](https://thequantuminsider.com/2021/05/12/swiss-based-qnami-closes-4-million-chf-4-4-million-u-s-series-a-funding-round/?utm_source=openai))

• Scaling and ecosystem challenges  
  As a deep-tech startup, Qnami faces hurdles in scaling production, building distribution channels, and supporting a broader ecosystem—especially as it transitions from research tools to industrial-grade instruments. ([oezratty.net](https://www.oezratty.net/wordpress/2025/decode-quantum-with-mathieu-munsch-from-qnami/?utm_source=openai))
